THIS R.P.F.C, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:8766  RPFC No. 100022 of 2022  ORDER The present petition is filed by the husband under Section 19(4) of the Family Courts Act,
challenging the Judgment dated 03.01.2022 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous No.340/2014 by the I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Hubballi (hereinafter referred to as 'the Family Court')
wherein, the petition filed by the wife under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code,
1973 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Cr.PC') claiming maintenance has been allowed and the husband has been directed to pay maintenance of Rs.4,000/-.
2.

The primary contention urged by the husband in the present petition is that, the finding of the Family Court that there was relationship of husband and wife between the parties was erroneous and on the said ground, the Judgment of the Family Court is required to be set aside.

3. It is noticed that, in the petition filed by the wife before the Family Court, the husband entered appearance and disputed the fact that the marriage NC: 2023:KHC-D:8766 between the parties took place on 29.10.2012 as alleged by the wife and that there was no subsisting relationship of husband and wife between the parties.

It was further contended by the husband that only an engagement ceremony had taken place between the parties and subsequent to the same, the husband came to know that the wife is a divorcee and she is suffering from various health ailments and hence,
whatever engagement that has taken place also was broken/terminated and he did not marry the petitioner/wife.
4. Consequent to the pleadings of the parties, the wife examined herself as P.W.1 and examined three witnesses as P.W.2 to P.W.5 and marked Ex.P.1 to P.14.
The husband examined himself as R.W.1 and marked Ex.R.1 to R.9.

The Family Court framed five points for consideration as follows:
(i) Whether the Petitioner proves that, she is a legally wedded wife of the Respondent and as on the date of filing of this petition, the relationship of her and the Respondent as that of legally wedded wife and husband is subsisting?
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8766 (ii) Whether the Petitioner proves that, the Respondent has given harassment and ill-treatment to her without any lawful reasons and cause as alleged ?

sentences.text: 2 (iii) Whether the Petitioner proves that, she is unable to maintain herself?
(iv) Whether the Petitioner proves that, the Respondent has willfully neglected and refused to maintain her in spite of having sufficient means as alleged ?
(v) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for maintenance from the Respondent as prayed for in the present petition ?
The Family Court vide Order dated 20.11.2021 permitted the husband to cross-examine the expert.
However, no steps were taken by the husband to pay requisite process fee to secure the presence of the expert for cross-examination;

(vi) As per the report of the expert it is clear that, the signatures on the Ex.P.10 i.e. application dated 16.09.2012 and Ex.P.12 i.e. application dated 25.09.2012 are the signatures of the husband;
(vii) P.W.4 is a Doctor who performed the abortion through DNC procedure.
Although the Doctor has been examined, no medical documents have been produced to NC: 2023:KHC-D:8766 show the DNC procedure conducted on the wife.
However, the Doctor has stated that the documents will be retained only for five years and will be destroyed thereafter, as the requisite rule stipulates maintenance of records only for five years.

P.W.4 is having her own hospital and she is running the hospital along with her husband and having adduced in oral evidence regarding the requisite details of the abortion procedure, the same was considered for the purpose of adjudication of the matter between the parties;
(viii) The wife has produced sufficient documents to demonstrate that she is legally wedded wife of the husband.

6. In view of the oral and documentary evidence on record, the Family Court has recorded a finding that, the marriage between the parties was solemnized on 29.10.2012 and is consummated and answered point No.1 in the affirmative.

The Family Court while considering the point No.2 has recorded the following findings :
(i) Ex.P.5, Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.7 i.e. certified copy of the FIR, complaint and charge-sheet in Crime No.64/2013 is the proceedings lodged against the husband by the wife for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323 and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.

sentences.text: (ii) Ex.P.9 is the certified copy of the Judgment dated 02.02.2021 passed in C.C.No.1144/2015 which discloses that the husband has been acquitted in the criminal case.
( iii )
It is clear from the material on record that, since 08.01.2013 the petitioner/wife and the respondent/husband are residing separately.
(iv) Hence, the Family Court has recorded a finding that, the wife was harassed and meted out with ill- treatment by the husband and answered point No.2 in the affirmative.
The Family Court while adjudicating upon the quantum of compensation has noticed that, the husband is performing Seva as Assistant Archaka in Huligemma Temple, Aravind Nagar, Old Hubballi.
The Family Court has also noticed that RW.1 in his cross-examination has admitted that he owns 3 commercial shops at Hubballi which fetches rentals.
Although the wife has contended that, the husband is earning `30,000/- from his work as an Assistant Archaka and `18,000/- from rental shops, no documents are produced to prove the same.

The Family Court after appreciating the evidence on record and having considered that he is working as an Assistant Archak as well as receiving rentals from the shops has awarded maintenance in a sum of Rs.4,000/- pm.

9. It is forthcoming from a re-appreciation of the material on record that the Family Court has appreciated in great detail the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the parties and in view of Exs.P1 to P4 as well as the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8766 oral evidence of the Doctor, PW.4 as also the other independent witnesses i.e., PWs.2, 3 and 5 has recorded the findings, as noticed above.
10.
It is relevant to note that the husband had contested his signatures at Exs.P10 and P12.
The Family Court relying on the opinion of the expert as well as the testimony of PW.5 has held that the signatures of the husband on the said documents are proved.
Further, the husband had disputed that Ex.P8 i.e., Marriage Invitation card is not pertaining to the parties.

The Family Court upon noticing the oral and documentary evidence as well as the relevant portions of Exs.R6, R7 and R8,
has recorded a categorical finding that the same is not sufficient to dispute the relationship of husband and wife as contended by the husband.
11. The Family Court has also noticed that the husband has not taken any other steps or initiated any other proceedings against the wife for falsely alleging that she is the wife of the Respondent.

sentences.text: 12. The proceedings initiated by the wife is under Section 125 of Cr.P.C.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Dwarika Prasad Satpathy Vs. Bidyut Prava Dixit1 has held that an order passed in an application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. does not finally determine the rights and obligations of the parties and the said section is enacted with a view to provide a summary remedy for providing maintenance to a wife, children and parents.

entities.text: Dwarika Prasad Satpathy Vs. Bidyut Prava Dixit1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajanesh Vs. Neha and another2 has held as follows:
"32. Chapter IX of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 provides for maintenance of wife, children and parents in a summary proceeding.
Maintenance under Section 125 CrPC may be claimed (1999) 7 SCC 675 (2021) 2 SCC 324 - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8766 by a person irrespective of the religious community to which they belong.
The purpose and object of Section 125 CrPC is to provide immediate relief to an applicant.
An application under Section 125 CrPC is predicated on two conditions: (i) the husband has sufficient means; and (ii) "neglects" to maintain his wife, who is unable to maintain herself.
In such a case, the husband may be directed by the Magistrate to pay such monthly sum to the wife, as deemed fit.
Maintenance is awarded on the basis of the financial capacity of the husband and other relevant factors.

33. The remedy provided by Section 125 is summary in nature, and the substantive disputes with respect to dissolution of marriage can be determined by a civil court/Family Court in an appropriate proceeding, such as the Hindu Marriage Act, 1956.
39. ...... Strict proof of marriage should not be a precondition for grant of maintenance under Section 125 Cr.PC. ............."
(Emphasis supplied)

14. Having regard to the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court as noticed above, the remedy under Section 125 being summary in nature, substantive disputes with respect of dissolution of marriage is required - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8766 to be determined in appropriate proceedings by Civil Courts/Family Courts.
Hence, there is no requirement for the Family Court to embark upon a detailed examination of facts as to the sufficiency of the causes for the wife to stay separately from the husband.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner has not demonstrated that the said finding recorded by the Family Court is without considering any particular material evidence on record in the absence of the same, it cannot be held that, the finding recorded by the Family Court regarding the relationship between the parties is erroneous and liable to be interfered by this Court.
16. With regard to the quantum of compensation, it is relevant to note that, admittedly the husband is working as an Assistant Archaka at Huligemma Temple as well as owning commercial shops.

Keeping in mind the intent behind Section 125 of Cr.P.C., which provides for a summary procedure for maintenance to be paid to wife, parents, etc., when they are destitute, having regard to - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8766 the fact that, the wife is staying separately and having regard to the fact that,
the wife is entitled to maintain herself with dignity, no ground is made out by the petitioner to demonstrate the quantum of maintenance awarded is erroneous or is excessive to warrant interference with the same by this Court.
17. In view of the same, the above petition is dismissed as being devoid of merit.
